description: It’s hard to keep a level head in a tough conversation, especially with someone you dislike. Veteran journalist Joshua Johnson — founding host of NPR's 1A, later anchor at MSNBC — argues the antidote isn't louder debate. It's better questions. Drawing from 20+ years in broadcast journalism including live broadcasts from CPAC, Johnson introduces "clinical journalism": a framework that replaces performative objectivity with genuine curiosity. He examines how asking about the story behind a belief — not just the belief itself — unlocks unexpected human connection. Three strategies, one radical reframe: objectivity isn't an identity. It's a skill anyone can learn. Joshua Johnson plays anchorman Dwight Richmond on the satirical Onion News Network. His portrayal helped The Onion win a 2025 Webby Award for Comedy. title: How to talk to people you dislike | Joshua Johnson | TEDxChicago

This talk is a blueprint for fearless living and proof that wherever your “dancefloor” resides, inner peace is available to us all.

Every single diaper ever made still exists today - and they take up to 500 years to break down. With 27 billion diapers dumped into U.S. landfills each year, the scale of plastic waste feels impossible. But what if the solution has been here all along - in fungi?

In this personal, surprising talk, serial entrepreneur Miki Agrawal (founder of THINX, TUSHY, and HIRO Diapers) shares how her team discovered a way to harness plastic-eating fungi to transform the world’s most wasteful product - the diaper - into something nature can reclaim. With humor, science, and storytelling, she invites us to reimagine waste not as the end of the story, but as the beginning of a new one.

Talk was given as part of the TEDx Global Idea Search.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What happens when an ordinary day is no longer ordinary? For millions of girls and women in Afghanistan, a simple walk to school has turned into an impossible dream. Since 2021, girls over the age of 11 have been banned from secondary education, erasing futures and silencing voices that the world desperately needs.
In this moving and urgent talk, Roquiya Sayeq shares Sarah’s story, one of many young women whose education was stripped away overnight. Yet amid the restrictions, a powerful movement is growing. Through an online educational center, Victory Afghanistan, Roquiya and her team are reclaiming lost learning hours.
But this fight extends beyond Afghanistan. Denying education to half a nation robs humanity of problem solvers, leaders, doctors, and innovators. This talk is both a call to action and a reminder: education equality is not optional; it is essential. What role will you play in ensuring every girl and woman has the chance to learn?

#Afghanistan #Women #Education #Activ
title: The Fight for Afghan Women’s Education | Roquiya Sayeq | TEDxChicago

In this thought-provoking talk, Afsha explores a quiet but powerful shift happening in storytelling, one we may not even realize we’re part of. As artificial intelligence becomes more embedded in the way we create and consume content, the lines between human imagination and machine-generated patterns are beginning to blur.

Drawing on real research, Afsha reveals how AI-generated writing can sometimes feel more “human” than what we create ourselves. But the real question isn’t about AI’s capabilities; it’s about us. Have we started to confuse familiarity with meaning? Are we responding to patterns rather than genuine human experience?

This talk challenges the idea that storytelling is purely about structure or technique. Instead, it brings us back to something deeper: intention. Because beyond the algorithms and outputs, what makes a story truly human is not how it sounds but why it exists.

Visit our website: https://www.tedxgiarre.com/ - Follow us on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/tedxgiarre/ Rosario Faraci  è Professore Ordinario di Economia e Gestione delle Imprese all’Università di Catania dove insegna Principi di Management e Business Model Innovation. E’ stato Presidente del corso di laurea in Economia Aziendale per cinque mandati e Delegato di Ateneo all’Imprenditorialità Accademica per 12 anni durante i mandati di tre diversi Rettori. Vincitore di una borsa di stud
title: Itaca non è più una destinazione | Rosario Faraci | TEDxGiarre

description: Başak Koç’un “Sahadan Hayata Bir Perspektif: Oyun Kurmaktan Anlam Kurmaya” başlıklı konuşması, spor sahasında kazanılan becerilerin hayatın geneline nasıl aktarıldığını ele alır. Koç, voleybolda oyun kurmanın yalnızca teknik bir süreç olmadığını, aynı zamanda hızlı karar alma, takım arkadaşlarını anlama ve sorumluluk üstlenme becerilerini içerdiğini vurgular. Bu deneyimlerin zamanla hayatın farklı alanlarında anlam kurma, hedef belirleme ve zorluklarla başa çıkma konusunda güçlü bir perspektif sunduğunu ifade eder. Ayrıca başarı ve başarısızlıkların sahadaki gibi hayatta da geçici olduğunu, asıl önemli olanın süreçten öğrenmek ve gelişime açık kalmak olduğunu belirtir. Konuşmanın temel mesajı, sporun sadece fiziksel değil, aynı zamanda zihinsel ve duygusal bir eğitim alanı olduğu ve bireyin hayata bakışını derinleştirdiğidir. . title: Neyi Korumalıyız, Neyi Terk Etmeliyiz? | Ayşegül Özer | TEDxAcibadem University

author: TEDx Talks
description: In this compelling and reflective talk, Kavita Krishnan delves into the idea of “permission” and how deeply it impacts our understanding of identity, belonging, and freedom. Drawing from personal encounters and broader social realities, she assesses how individuals are often presumed to seek approval from families, institutions, and society at large; simply to exercise individual agency about love, life, and self-expression. Through striking recollections and transformative narratives, she questions whether democracy should be articulated by the voice of the majority or by the preservation of individual rights. For Kavita, being human is not a static identity but a lifelong pursuit - one that requires fortitude, compassion, and the readiness to allow others the same liberty we strive for ourselves. title: Marriage, majority, and democracy | Kavita Krishnan | TEDxMirandaHouse

author: TEDx Talks
description: A student explores how smartphones, while essential to modern life, can quietly take control of our time and attention. Through research with her peers and personal reflection, she reveals how excessive screen use impacts focus, sleep, and mental health. By making small changes in her own habits, she shows that it is possible to regain control and reconnect with what truly matters. In a world full of notifications, she challenges us to ask: who is really in control—us or our devices?
